\brandsection{Overview}
{\large This is an indicative component set for Your Brand — enough to give a feel for how the interface will look, not a full production kit. Every component uses the shared token palette, so it matches the brand guide. Replace the placeholder tokens in component-build/components.py with your own and re-run to regenerate this document.}\par\vspace{4mm}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Buttons} — variants, sizes, and states.
\item \textbf{Form controls} — inputs, selection, and toggles.
\item \textbf{Badges \& alerts} — status indicators and messages.
\item \textbf{Cards} — contained content surfaces.
\item \textbf{Navigation} — navbar, tabs, breadcrumb, pagination.
\item \textbf{Avatars \& feedback} — identity and progress elements.
\end{itemize}
\clearpage

\brandsection{Buttons}

Buttons trigger actions. Use one primary action per section; lower-emphasis actions take the
secondary or ghost style. Every button keeps a minimum 44 x 44 px touch target.

\subhead{Variants}
\uibtn[primary]{Primary}\quad\uibtnoutline[primary]{Secondary}\quad\uibtnghost[primary]{Ghost}\quad\uibtn[accent]{Accent}\quad\uibtn[error]{Delete}\quad\uibtn[success]{Confirm}\par
\vspace{2mm}
{\small\color{muted}One primary action per section; secondary and ghost for lower-emphasis actions.}\par

\subhead{Sizes}
\uibtnsm[primary]{Small}\quad\uibtn[primary]{Default}\quad\uibtnlg[primary]{Large}\par

\subhead{States}
\uibtn[primary]{Default}\quad\uibtn[accent]{Hover}\quad\uibtn[muted]{Disabled}\par
\vspace{2mm}
{\small\color{muted}Icon-only buttons require an accessible label; disabled buttons drop to a muted fill.}\par

\clearpage

\brandsection{Form Controls}

Form controls capture user input. Every field pairs a clear label with a bordered
control; state is communicated through border colour and supporting text rather than
colour alone, to satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA.

{\small\color{muted} Border colour signals state: neutral (default), accent (focus),
error (invalid). Never rely on colour as the sole cue.}

\vspace{4mm}
\subhead{Text Input}

\brandsection{Badges \& Chips}

Badges and chips are compact, non-interactive (or lightly interactive) labels. Use \textbf{solid badges} to communicate fixed status, and \textbf{soft chips} for removable tags and filter selections.

\vspace{2mm}

\subhead{Status badges}

\uibadge[primary]{Project}\quad\uibadge[success]{Active}\quad\uibadge[warning]{Pending}\quad\uibadge[error]{Overdue}\quad\uibadge[info]{Info}

\vspace{2mm}
{\small\color{muted} Solid, white-text badges carry a single word of state. Map colour to meaning consistently: primary for neutral identity, success for healthy, warning for attention, error for blocking, info for advisory.}

\vspace{5mm}

\subhead{Chips / tags}

\uichip{Design}\quad\uichip{Frontend}\quad\uichip{GDPR}\quad\uichip{SEO}

\vspace{2mm}
{\small\color{muted} Soft outlined chips label removable tags and active filters. They read as lighter than badges, invite dismissal (an 'x' affordance in the live component), and can wrap freely across a filter bar.}

\vspace{5mm}

\subhead{When to use which}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=5mm,itemsep=1mm]
  \item \textbf{Badge} -- fixed, system-owned status the user cannot remove (Active, Overdue).
  \item \textbf{Chip} -- user-owned, removable selection: applied filters, assigned tags, chosen categories.
  \item Keep labels to one or two words; never sentence-length. Prefer a tooltip for detail.
\end{itemize}

\clearpage

\brandsection{Alerts}

Alerts communicate a page-level status or system message to the reader. Each alert pairs a
coloured frame and title with a soft tinted background, so the message reads clearly without
competing with the surrounding content. Use them for feedback that applies to the whole page or
a completed action.

\vspace{2mm}

\subhead{Alert Variants}

\vspace{1mm}

\uialert{info}{infobg}{Information}{A short informational message for the reader.}

\vspace{2mm}

\uialert{success}{successbg}{Success}{Your changes have been saved successfully.}

\vspace{2mm}

\uialert{warning}{warningbg}{Caution}{This action may take a few minutes to complete.}

\vspace{2mm}

\uialert{error}{errorbg}{Error}{Something went wrong. Please try again.}

\vspace{3mm}

{\small\color{muted} Alerts are for page-level messages, not inline field validation. Reserve the
error variant for genuine failures, and pair the success variant with an action the reader has
just completed.}

\clearpage

\brandsection{Cards}

Cards group related content into a bordered container. Compose them in fixed-width minipages to build a responsive grid; keep body copy short so cards in a row align in height.

\vspace{3mm}
\subhead{Card grid}

\vspace{1mm}
\noindent
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.31\linewidth}
\begin{uicard}
\textcolor{accent}{\textbf{Feature}}\\[1mm]
{\large\textbf{Fast delivery}}\\[1.5mm]
{\small We ship production-ready builds in tight, predictable cycles.}\\[1mm]
{\small Every release is reviewed, tested, and documented.}\\[2mm]
\uibtnghost[accent]{Learn more}
\end{uicard}
\end{minipage}%
\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.31\linewidth}
\begin{uicard}
\textit{``A short client quote about the work.''}\\[3mm]
\uiavatar[secondary]{AB}\ \ \textbf{Alex Brown}\\
{\small\color{muted}Director, Acme}\\[2mm]
{\small A dependable partner from first call to launch day.}
\end{uicard}
\end{minipage}%
\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.31\linewidth}
\begin{uicard}
\colorbox{panel}{\makebox[\linewidth][c]{\rule{0pt}{14mm}}}\\[2mm]
\uichip{Web}\ \uichip{SEO}\\[2mm]
\textbf{A headline}\\[1mm]
{\small How we grew organic traffic for a national brand.}\\[2mm]
\uibtnghost[accent]{Read case study}
\end{uicard}
\end{minipage}

\vspace{3mm}
{\small\color{muted}Three card patterns: a feature card with a call to action, a testimonial card with an avatar identity, and a case-study card with a media placeholder and category chips. Each sits in a 0.31\,\textbackslash linewidth minipage separated by \textbackslash hfill.}

\clearpage

\brandsection{Avatars \& Feedback}

Identity markers, progress indicators, and loading placeholders. Avatars carry initials in a rounded square; progress and skeleton components share the same bar primitive at different fills.

\subhead{Avatars}

A single avatar renders the member's initials on a coloured tile.

\vspace{2mm}
\uiavatar[accent]{SB}
\vspace{2mm}

{\small\color{muted}Single avatar, accent tile with initials.}

\vspace{4mm}

Stacked into a group row, avatars summarise a team; the trailing muted tile counts the overflow.

\vspace{2mm}

\vspace{2mm}

{\small\color{muted}Avatar group -- three members plus a '+3' overflow tile.}
